title: Drug exam
description: Every medicine: effect, dose, route, dangers, antidotes.

questions.q: What is Ketamine (Calypsol)?
answers: An induction agent (RSI step 1), a painkiller in small doses
A muscle relaxant (RSI step 2), a sedative in small doses
A strong opioid painkiller that Naloxone can reverse
A sedative for seizures and stimulant agitation

questions.q: How does Ketamine affect the blood pressure?
answers: It keeps or raises it, so it is good in shock
It lowers it strongly, so avoid it in shock
It lowers it a little, like every sedative
It has no effect at all on the circulation

questions.q: What is the painkilling dose of Ketamine?
What does Rocuronium do?
answers: It paralyses the muscles and stops the breathing: only with sedation and intubation
It puts the patient to sleep and relaxes the muscles, so it is enough alone for RSI
It sedates the patient but keeps the breathing, so it is safe for agitation
It relaxes the airway muscles and is used for a severe asthma attack

questions.q: What happens if an awake patient gets Rocuronium?
answers: They stay conscious but cannot move or breathe: panic, a serious error
They fall asleep within a minute, so the sedative is no longer needed
Only the limbs relax, the breathing muscles keep working normally
Nothing, Rocuronium only works together with Ketamine or Midazolam

questions.q: What is Fentanyl for?
What is the usual dose of Fentanyl?
Sign and antidote of a Fentanyl overdose?
answers: Agitation, fast pulse, wide pupils – Naloxone

questions.q: Dose of Adrenaline in cardiac arrest?
What is a push-dose of Adrenaline?
answers: A very small dose (about 0.02 mg) for low blood pressure around an arrest
The full 1 mg dose pushed fast through the IV during cardiac arrest
A double dose (2 mg) when the first one did not bring back the pulse
A small dose (about 0.2 mg) into the muscle for a severe allergy

questions.q: What does Adrenaline do?
answers: Raises the pulse and the blood pressure, improves the chance of ROSC
Slows the pulse and lowers the blood pressure, calms the heart
Raises the blood pressure but slows the pulse, protects the heart
Stabilises the rhythm and stops VF without the need for a shock

questions.q: How do you give Captopril?
What is the usual dose of Nitroglycerin spray?
What is the usual dose of Glucose 40%?
What is the usual dose of glucose gel?
What does Insulin do?
answers: Slowly lowers a very high blood glucose
Quickly lowers any high blood glucose
Raises a low blood glucose more slowly
Replaces fluid lost from high glucose

questions.q: What is the biggest danger of Insulin?
answers: A steep fall of the blood pressure

questions.q: Do you give Insulin to an unconscious patient with an unknown blood glucose?
answers: Yes, if the patient is a known diabetic
Yes, a half dose to be on the safe side
Yes, if the breath smells of acetone

questions.q: What is the usual dose of Naloxone?
answers: 4 mg nasal spray (2 mg is the smaller one)
0.4 mg nasal spray (0.2 mg is the smaller one)
4 mg IV only (2 mg is the smaller one)
40 mg nasal spray (20 mg is the smaller one)

questions.q: What is the dose of Salbutamol?
An asthmatic patient's chest is “silent”, you barely hear any breathing. What does it mean?
answers: Life threatening: hardly moving air – immediate treatment, ALS
Improvement: the Salbutamol opened the airways, keep watching
Normal after an attack: the patient is tired, let them rest
Hyperventilation: the patient breathes too fast to hear it

questions.q: What is Midazolam (Dormicum) for?
answers: Sedation: agitation from cocaine / amphetamine, seizures
Pain relief: fractures and burns, with Fentanyl together
Muscle relaxation: RSI step 2, after the induction agent

questions.q: What is the danger of Midazolam?
answers: Depressed breathing and low blood pressure
Agitation and a fast pulse, mainly in the elderly
High blood pressure and a slow pulse

questions.q: What is the usual dose of Midazolam?
What does dosing per kg mean?
answers: The dose is multiplied by the body weight (80 kg × 1 mcg = 80 mcg)
The dose is divided by the body weight (80 mcg ÷ 80 kg = 1 mcg)
The dose is given once for every 10 kg of body weight
Every adult gets the dose of an average 70 kg adult

questions.q: Sleeping pill (benzodiazepine) overdose, often with alcohol. What is the basis of prehospital care?
answers: Naloxone spray, repeated until the patient wakes
Glucose 40% IV, alcohol lowers the blood glucose
Push-dose Adrenaline to wake the patient up

questions.q: Which medicine treats stimulant (cocaine, amphetamine) poisoning?
Which one can you NOT give without an IV?
RSI dose of Ketamine (1.5 mg/kg) for an 80 kg patient?
What happens if you give several doses of the same medicine in a short time?
answers: The doses add up and can lead to an overdose
Only the last dose works, the earlier ones fade
The body gets used to it, so the effect drops
Nothing: the safe limit is the same per dose
